parsed.draft_response:
Hi — I’m sorry this is blocking your client launch. Since the project was deleted and you used the in-retention restore, but some files and comments are still missing, we’ll need to escalate to our engineering team to review the restore outcome for your specific project.

To help us investigate quickly, could you please reply with the following details?
1) Project identifier (project name and/or ID) and which workspace/environment it should be in after restore.
2) The exact items still missing (file names/paths and comment identifiers, if available), plus what is currently present.
3) Approximate timestamps: when the project was deleted (yesterday—time/timezone if you have it) and when restore was triggered (and time/timezone), if shown in your activity/audit logs.
4) Confirm that the restore you clicked was the standard “Restore” action for deleted items within the retention window (any wording shown in the UI).

If you can, also include any screenshots of the restore confirmation screen or the project view showing what’s missing.

Once we have the above, we’ll route it to engineering for deeper recovery investigation. We understand this is critical given the Monday deadline, and we’ll prioritize your case accordingly.
promised_actions: Escalate the case to engineering to review why the restore did not fully recover the project contents
safety_notes: We cannot confirm recovery completeness or root cause from the information provided; we are requesting the minimum details needed for engineering investigation.
No refund, SLA, or guarantee of restoration is promised.
